manifesto.title: INK FIRST. COLOR SECOND. POCKET ALWAYS.
body: 36TY is a Brooklyn producer building records the way 1994 built comics: thick ink, loud color, no apology. The drums are boom-bap — dusty, swung, slightly behind the beat on purpose. The harmony is R&B — minor-7 silk, gospel inversions, chords that sit in the chest.

The alias started as a late-night crate ritual. MPC 2000XL. A milk crate of '92–'99 vinyl. A cheap Rhodes plugin that got replaced by the real thing. Now the booth is a full room and the sound is still the same argument: the snare has to knock, the hook has to melt.
Not nostalgia. Archaeology with a new mix bus. 90s hip-hop grammar, 90s comic framing, 2026 low-end.

tapes.title: SILK ON THE 808
tapes.blurb: Velvet Rhodes, a kicked-in 808, and a snare that sounds like a comic punch. After-hours R&B with boom-bap posture.

tapes.title: BOOTH TAPE VOL. 3
tapes.blurb: Raw MPC bounce. Chopped horns, vinyl crackle, and a kick that sits in the gutter. The working tape — no polish pass.

tapes.title: AFTER HOURS CHORDS
tapes.blurb: Slow-jam architecture. Gospel voicings, tape delay, a bassline that talks. Built for 2am vocals.

tapes.title: CRATE DIG '97
tapes.blurb: The archaeology joint. Filtered break, chopped '97 soul, boom-bap swing at 97. Head-nod mandatory.

studio.title: MPC IN THE CORNER. VINYL ON THE FLOOR.
studio.body: The booth is a Bed-Stuy walk-up with too many cables and the right amount of ugly. MPC 2000XL for the chops. Live Rhodes when the plugin lies. A pair of old Yamahas that still tell the truth. Sessions are booked in blocks — drums first, silk second, hook last.

booking.title: CUSTOM BEATS. SESSIONS. SYNC.
booking.body: Beat leases, exclusive buys, topline sessions, and trailer cues. 36TY does not do moodboard-as-a-service. Send a reference, a tempo, and the feeling. The pocket does the rest.
booking.formNote: Serious inquiries only. If the email is a paragraph, it gets a paragraph back.
